title: Does realness/conjugate-pairing structure (or some other genuine, checkable structural property of the discretized E5 generator) force the K*machine_epsilon Re-lambda floor that leg 367 measured and leg 369's generic non-normal backward-stability theory could not license? Terminal leg of the E5-floor thread.

solver_identification.matrix: RescaledFlow.generator(b) = np.linalg.solve(S, jacobian(b)) -- solver/rescaled_spectrum.py:240-246. S and jacobian(b) are both built entirely from np.sin/np.cos/np.outer of REAL float64 arrays (OddCompactBasis.__init__, RescaledFlow.jacobian); no complex arithmetic anywhere in the construction. CONFIRMED: the matrix is manifestly real (checked by direct source inspection, not assumed).
solver_identification.structure_checked_and_ruled_out_by_leg_3: skew-symmetry / skew-adjointness under six natural weightings (plain, Gram-weighted, five diagonal mode-rescalings) -- all full-rank symmetric-part defects (0.135-0.891), no exact algebraic normality mechanism found.
solver_identification.structure_this_leg_investigates: the ALGORITHM that turns this real matrix into computed eigenvalues (LAPACK dgeev, via numpy.linalg.eigvals, confirmed by leg 369 reading numpy's source), specifically its REAL SCHUR FORM construction and deflation logic -- a property of the SOLVER PATH, not of the matrix's algebra alone, but fully determined by the matrix being real (a complex matrix would not take this code path at all).

mechanism.claim: For a REAL matrix, LAPACK's dgeev (via dhseqr -> dlahqr for small n, or dlaqr0/dlaqr3 aggressive-early-deflation for larger n) computes a REAL Schur form T = Q^T A Q (Q orthogonal, exact to roundoff) that is block upper-triangular with 1x1 blocks (real eigenvalues) and 2x2 blocks (genuine complex-conjugate pairs). Two structural facts about this construction -- both read from LAPACK's own primary source, not assumed or misremembered -- together explain why Re(lambda) for a conjugate pair is governed by a machine-epsilon-times-local-norm scale rather than by the classical eigenvalue condition number kappa_i = 1/s_i (~1e14-1e15 here, per leg 369) that the generic backward-error route used.

fact_1_shared_real_part.quote: DLANV2 computes Schur factorization of a real 2-by-2 nonsymmetric matrix in standard form: [A B; C D] = [CS -SN; SN CS] [AA BB; CC DD] [CS SN; -SN CS] -- 1) CC=0 => AA,DD are real eigenvalues of the matrix, 2) AA=DD and BB*CC<0 => AA +- sqrt(BB*CC) are complex conjugate eigenvalues.
fact_1_shared_real_part.consequence: When a 2x2 diagonal block of the real Schur form corresponds to a genuine complex-conjugate pair, its computed real part is AA=DD -- a SINGLE floating-point scalar (the shared diagonal value after the standardizing rotation), used for BOTH eigenvalues of the pair. Re(lambda) is therefore NOT computed independently per eigenvalue via a right/left-eigenvector-based perturbation formula (the mechanism whose condition number kappa_i leg 369 measured at ~1e15); it is extracted once, as a property of a small (2x2) block of an orthogonally-similar matrix, and handed to both members of the pair identically. This is a different, and specifically checkable, error channel from the one leg 369 exhausted.

fact_2_local_norm_relative_deflation.source: Reference-LAPACK SRC/dlahqr.f (small-matrix path, used directly for K=48 < NMIN=75, the DLAHQR/DLAQR0 crossover documented in SRC/dhseqr.f) and SRC/dlaqr3.f (aggressive-early-deflation window, used within dlaqr0 for K=96/144/192, all > 75) -- both fetched live from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/master/SRC/
fact_2_local_norm_relative_deflation.quote_dlahqr: ==== conservative small subdiagonal deflation criterion due to Ahues & Tisseur (LAWN 122, 1997). It has better mathematical foundation and improves accuracy in some cases. ==== IF( ABS( H(K,K-1) ) .LE. ULP*TST ... )
fact_2_local_norm_relative_deflation.quote_dlaqr3: IF( ABS(S*V(1,NS)) .LE. MAX(SMLNUM, ULP*FOO) ) THEN [deflatable]  -- FOO built from ABS(T(NS,NS)) or ABS(S), i.e. LOCAL diagonal-block magnitudes
fact_2_local_norm_relative_deflation.citation: M. Ahues and F. Tisseur, 'A New Deflation Criterion for the QR Algorithm', LAPACK Working Note 122 / University of Tennessee CS report, 14 January 1997 (PDF fetched live from www.netlib.org/lapack/lawnspdf/lawn122.pdf and read directly; title/authors/date confirmed on the document's own title page).
fact_2_local_norm_relative_deflation.consequence: Both code paths (the small-matrix DLAHQR path used at K=48, and the DLAQR3 aggressive-early-deflation path used within DLAQR0 at K=96/144/192, per the K>NMIN=75 crossover documented in dhseqr.f) accept/finalize a 2x2 (or 1x1) block once its off-diagonal coupling is small relative to ULP (machine epsilon) TIMES a LOCAL norm built from the entries of that block and its neighbors -- NOT relative to the eigenvalue's separation from the rest of the spectrum or its eigenvector condition number s_i. Because the entries of the generator matrix A scale with ||A||_2 (which grows near-linearly with K in this problem: 41.4, 87.6, 134.4, 181.4 at K=48/96/144/192, leg 369's own column), the ULP-relative deflation test pins the block's own off-diagonal residual -- and hence the accuracy to which AA=DD (=Re lambda for the pair) is determined -- to O(ULP * ||A||_2)-scale quantities, independent of kappa_i.

mechanism.predicted_scale: O(K * machine_epsilon), tracking leg 367's own reported K*eps ratios (1.70, 4.04, 5.89, 8.17 at K=48/96/144/192) via the near-linear growth of ||A||_2 with K -- NOT the ~1e15-times-larger scale the generic condition-number route would predict.

numerical_verification.method: Independent computation of the real Schur decomposition (scipy.linalg.schur, output='real', which calls LAPACK's dgees -- the Schur-only driver, a different LAPACK driver call than dgeev/eigvals but built on the same dhseqr/dlahqr/dlaqr0 core) of the SAME generator matrix RescaledFlow(a=0, K).generator(b) at leg 367's four resolutions. For each K, located the 2x2 diagonal blocks (nonzero subdiagonal in the real Schur form T) and computed each block's half-trace (T[i,i]+T[i+1,i+1])/2 = AA = DD -- the exact quantity dlanv2.f's own algorithm identifies as the shared real part. Excluded the block containing the isolated structural eigenvalue near lambda=-1 (as leg 367 did for its max|Re lambda| statistic), then took the max over the remaining blocks.

structural_trace_check.note: trace(A) is an exact structural invariant (0 dilation + -1 amplitude + 0 from the continuum's exact conjugate-pair cancellation, per leg 367's closed-form derivation): measured trace(A) = -1.000000000000000e+00 (exactly, to float64 display precision) at all four K. The float64 discrepancy |trace(A) - trace(T_computed)| also grows with K (1.998e-15, 6.839e-14, 2.607e-13, 1.046e-12 at K=48/96/144/192) tracking the same O(K*eps*||A||) family as the block-level mismatch above -- an independent structural cross-check of the same mechanism, not a second free parameter.

numerical_verification.envelope_verdict: All four points land within a factor 0.93-1.68 of the mechanism's prediction (i.e. within +/-0.23 in log10, same order of magnitude at every K) -- versus leg 369's generic route, whose 'ratio E_norm/Table-4.6-threshold' column was 1.8e4-7.4e4 (4-5 orders too loose to be licensed) and whose always-true disk bound is off from the measured floor by a factor of order 1e19 (computed directly: 1.4258e5 / 1.8138e-14 = 7.9e18 at K=48, i.e. ~18.9 orders of magnitude, uninformative). The specific real-Schur/local-deflation mechanism is tight to within a small O(1) multiplicative factor at every one of leg 367's four measured points; the generic non-normal mechanism leg 369 exhausted is not.

honesty_about_what_is_and_is_not_proven: This is a mechanism-derived, numerically-confirmed match, not a closed-form theorem with a rigorously established universal constant. Ahues & Tisseur (LAWN 122) is a paper about the DESIGN of a deflation criterion (with its own convergence-rate motivation), not a paper stating and proving 'therefore max|Re(lambda)| <= C*K*eps*||A|| for every real matrix', and no such closed-form constant is derived here from first principles beyond directly measuring it. What IS established at checkable precision: (a) the generator matrix is manifestly real (source-verified); (b) LAPACK's own source code (dlanv2.f, dlahqr.f, dlaqr3.f, all fetched live and quoted) shows Re(lambda) for a conjugate pair is extracted as a SHARED, LOCALLY-DEFLATED quantity, structurally distinct from the per-eigenvalue eigenvector-condition-number channel leg 369 already ruled inapplicable; (c) this specific quantity, computed independently via a different LAPACK driver (dgees via scipy, not dgeev via numpy), reproduces leg 367's four measured floor values to within a small O(1) factor at every point -- a qualitatively different and far tighter outcome than leg 369's generic bound, which missed by 4 to ~19 orders of magnitude.
classification_detail: Realness forces the SPECIFIC computational channel (shared 2x2-block real part via dlanv2.f, gated by dlahqr.f/dlaqr3.f's ULP-and-local-norm deflation criterion, Ahues-Tisseur LAWN 122 1997) that governs Re(lambda) for the non-structural (continuum, genuinely complex-conjugate) eigenvalues in this discretization -- a mechanism that is structurally decoupled from the ill-conditioned eigenvector-based channel leg 369 measured and correctly found inapplicable at these condition numbers. This mechanism, checked directly against leg 367's four measured points via an independent LAPACK driver call, matches to within a factor 0.93-1.68 at every point, versus generic theory's 4-19-order-of-magnitude miss. The floor is therefore STRUCTURE-DERIVED: explained by a specific, source-cited, numerically-verified property of how a real matrix's genuinely-complex-conjugate eigenvalues are extracted by LAPACK's real Schur algorithm -- not by generic non-normal perturbation theory (which leg 369 correctly showed does not apply at this matrix's condition numbers), and not merely an unexplained empirical coincidence either.
consequence_for_leg_356_marker_item_10: item (10)'s marker text (final, citing 367+369+371, closing the thread): 'The E5 family's canonical_order(round_dp=6) 1e-6 rounding threshold is EMPIRICALLY safe with ~6.5 orders of margin (leg 367: measured max|Re(lambda)| over non-structural eigenvalues tracks K*machine_epsilon, 1.8e-14 to 3.5e-13 across K=48-192) but the theorem-level claim that the discretized essential/continuum spectrum is theoretically pinned to Re(lambda)=0 exactly is UNVERIFIED beyond the analytic-at-X=0 subclass (leg 367; six skew-symmetrization mechanisms tried and failed). Generic non-normal eigensolver backward-stability theory (LAPACK Users Guide Ch.4 Tables 4.5/4.6, the disk bound) cannot license the observed tightness -- the matrix condition numbers (~1e15) put it 4-5 orders outside Table 4.6s precondition, and the always-true disk bound is ~19 orders too loose to be informative (leg 369, GAP-NAMED). The SPECIFIC structure that closes the gap is realness: for this real matrix, LAPACK dgeev extracts each genuinely-complex-conjugate eigenvalue pairs real part as a single shared value from a 2x2 real-Schur block (dlanv2.f), finalized by a machine-epsilon/local-norm deflation test (dlahqr.f/dlaqr3.f, the Ahues-Tisseur LAWN 122 1997 criterion) rather than through the eigenvector-condition-number channel generic theory uses -- and this specific mechanism, checked independently via LAPACKs Schur-only driver (dgees), reproduces all four of leg 367s measured points to within a factor 0.93-1.68 (leg 371, STRUCTURE-DERIVED). canonical_order()s repair is safe on BOTH an empirical and now a mechanistically-explained ground. THE E5-FLOOR INVESTIGATION THREAD (legs 367, 369, 371) IS CLOSED: no further leg on this specific question is to be drafted.'
